_comment: verify-gate-enforcement manifest — closes catalog class G1 (gate-enforcement vacuity) from docs/verification/fv-adversarial-review-playbook.md Part A2. Each soundness/anti-vacuity gate declares WHAT source surface it polices, WHICH workflow must run it, and its ENFORCEMENT level. check_gate_enforcement.py asserts the live CI wiring matches — a gate that is green-when-run but never RUNS on the diff it polices (wrong `paths:` filter, `continue-on-error`, workflow_dispatch-only, or unwired) is exactly as dangerous as a hollow proof (the 2026-07-01 F1 finding: verify-ledger-consistency never fired on AXIOM_STATUS.json-only edits). enforcement: 'per_pr_blocking' = must run on push/pull_request, non-continue-on-error, and the trigger `paths:` must COVER polices_paths; 'nightly' = must be invoked by a scheduled workflow; 'local_documented' = deliberately not CI-gated (a NOTE, never a failure) — must carry a `why`. polices_paths are repo-relative prefixes/globs the gate is responsible for.

Zero-width (U+200B..U+200F/U+FEFF) and bidi override/isolate (U+202A..U+202E, U+2066..U+2069) codepoints are invisible to git diff and to code review. Two attacks share that mechanism: TrapDoor-style poisoning of the AI-instruction files every coding agent executes, and Trojan Source (CVE-2021-42574). Baseline 2026-07-31 is ZERO hits over 3841 tracked text files with NO allowlist — the two pre-existing hits were fixed, not exempted, because an allowlist here is a place to hide the payload. Carries a two-sided self-test (5 payload classes fire, 3 benign inputs stay silent); ordinary non-ASCII is deliberately allowed or the gate would be red on day one and disabled by the end of the week.

gates.why: The three 100-byte-symbolic multiSend harnesses (per_record_page_bound 12.71 GiB/6m03s, no_hidden_value 13.05 GiB/7m55s, cow_presign_precedence 11.50 GiB/3m56s; all VERIFY SUCCESSFULLY, measured locally 2026-07-31) exceed what a hosted runner can absorb. Instrumented CI evidence 2026-07-31: the runner has 15,989 MB RAM with 14,497 MB available and 145 GB disk with 86 GB free, so DISK IS NOT THE CAUSE - it is memory. The kill lands between 'Runtime Postprocess Equation' and 'Solving with ...', i.e. inside CBMC's formula construction and BEFORE any SAT solver is invoked; a kissat experiment was therefore reverted, since the solver never runs. (That experiment's local peak-RSS numbers were also unsound: an external solver runs out-of-process and /usr/bin/time -v reports a per-process maximum, not an aggregate.) Excluded because an OOM kills the runner and suppresses every later mandatory gate in the same job - same reasoning as verify-extracted-heavy (53c19f21); continue-on-error cannot save a dead runner. The 100-byte bound is deliberately NOT reduced: shrinking a proof's bound to earn a green check is coverage loss disguised as a pass. Larger hosted runners are unavailable (Team/Enterprise-only; this org is free-plan; hosted-runners API 404s). Run via `make kani-heavy`; the other 170 harnesses stay blocking in nightly.
